title: Manager Communication & Coaching Skills
description: Practice handling difficult conversations with employees

scenarios.customerSays: An employee says your feedback in a meeting felt harsh and made them question their ability.
scenarios.question: How do you respond?

options.text: Listen to their concern, validate their feeling, explain your intent, and reconnect on what you meant.
options.feedback: ✓ Masterful! You showed empathy while clarifying your good intent. You acknowledged their feeling AND explained the facts. This rebuilds trust.

options.text: Explain that you were just being direct and they need to handle feedback better.
options.feedback: ❌ You're right about intent, but wrong about impact. Their feeling is valid. Try: 'I appreciate you telling me. That wasn't my intent. Let me explain...'

options.text: Apologize and say you'll soften your feedback in the future.
options.feedback: ⚠️ Your heart's in the right place, but you're swinging too far. Honest feedback matters. Try: 'I'm sorry it felt harsh. I meant to help you improve. Let's discuss...'

scenarios.customerSays: Two strong personalities on your team are clashing. It's affecting team morale.
scenarios.question: What's your first move?

options.text: Have 1-on-1 conversations with each person separately to understand their perspective before any group conversation.
options.feedback: Perfect! Individual conversations first let each person vent without the other person getting defensive. You gather facts, show you care, then mediate informed.

options.text: Call a team meeting and have them work it out publicly.
options.feedback: ❌ Public conflict escalates tension. Private 1-on-1s first. Only bring people together when you understand both sides AND you know how to mediate.

options.text: Tell them both to get along or there will be consequences.
options.feedback: ⚠️ Authority doesn't solve personality clashes. Listen first, understand the real issue, then address it. Try: 'Tell me what's happening from your perspective.'

scenarios.customerSays: One of your best performers has been missing deadlines and their work quality is slipping. You notice they seem distracted.
scenarios.question: What's your approach?

options.text: Have a private conversation: 'I've noticed X. How are you doing? What's going on?' Listen before jumping to conclusions.
options.feedback: Excellent! You led with curiosity, not judgment. Maybe they're dealing with something personal. Listen first, then help. This shows you care about the person, not just the performance.

options.text: Put them on a performance improvement plan immediately.
options.feedback: ❌ You're rushing to discipline when you should be asking questions. Is this a personal issue, a skill gap, or a motivation problem? Find out first.

options.text: Assign them less important work until they get back on track.
options.feedback: ⚠️ You're making assumptions. Talk to them first! They might have a valid reason (family issue, health problem, confusion about priorities). Ask.

scenarios.customerSays: You have a project that's beyond someone's current experience, but you believe they can do it with support.
scenarios.question: How do you delegate it?

options.text: Tell them why you think they're ready, offer support and resources, set a timeline for check-ins, and let them know it's okay to ask questions.
options.feedback: Perfect! You're coaching them up, not just throwing them in. Clear expectations, safety net (check-ins), and psychological safety (okay to ask). This builds confidence AND capability.

options.text: Give them the assignment and tell them to figure it out.
options.feedback: ❌ That's sink or swim. They might drown and lose confidence. Stretch assignments need support. Try: 'You're ready for this. Here's how I'll help...'

options.text: Give them the assignment but warn them it's hard and might not work out.
options.feedback: ⚠️ You're undermining their confidence before they start. Instead: 'This is a great learning opportunity. I believe you can do this, and here's my support...'

masteryLevels.label: Exceptional Manager 🏆
masteryLevels.description: You handle tough conversations with empathy, wisdom, and clarity. Your team trusts you, grows under you, and stays engaged. This is leadership excellence.

masteryLevels.label: Strong Communicator 💼
masteryLevels.description: You handle most conversations well and show genuine care for your team. Focus on the scenarios where you scored lower to strengthen your skills.

masteryLevels.label: Developing Leadership 📈
masteryLevels.description: You're building your communication skills. Difficult conversations are hard. Review the scenarios you found challenging and practice with a mentor or manager.

masteryLevels.label: Leadership Development Recommended 🎓
masteryLevels.description: Managing people requires specific communication skills. Consider taking a management training course or working with a leadership coach on difficult conversations.
